title: NSFOCUS: new Cling botnet variant hides command traffic in public STUN services
date_note: NSFOCUS's post gives only its publication day; it says CNCERT detected the variant in November 2026.
geo_basis: country of the publisher and of CNCERT, the detector named in the post; no victim location stated
summary: NSFOCUS says CNCERT detected the widespread propagation of a new variant of the Cling botnet in November 2026. NSFOCUS says the variant conceals its command-and-control among public STUN services and primarily spreads by exploiting CVE-2021-3539. It says daily active bots peaked at 2,730, with a cumulative total of 5,600 infected devices, and that the variant removes its DDoS, proxy and propagation modules.
plain: NSFOCUS says a new version of the Cling botnet is spreading, hiding its control traffic in public STUN services; it counts a cumulative total of 5,600 infected devices.
exec: NSFOCUS reports a Cling botnet variant with a cumulative total of 5,600 infected devices, peaking at 2,730 active bots a day.
action: NSFOCUS advises patching known vulnerabilities, updating IoT firmware, using strong unique passwords, and monitoring for anomalous STUN traffic and suspicious startup entries.

evidence.quote: the number of bots infected by this botnet and active on a daily basis peaked at 2,730
with a cumulative total of 5,600 infected devices.

validation.note: Only NSFOCUS's own post was read; Security Boulevard republishes the same NSFOCUS text, so it is one publisher.

review.note: Compared title, date, CNCERT detection, STUN C2, CVE, 2,730 and 5,600 figures, action against NSFOCUS post
